report:
Summary
- The evidence supports a real difference: the B−A residual activation difference pushes logits toward tokens in the “culinary/restaurant/cooking” and “professional/academic” lexical domains. In other words, Model B shows stronger internal activation toward words like restaurant/Cooking/Chef/baking/kitchen and toward words like dissertation/professional/Professional/metropolitan, especially in middle-to-late layers and early token positions.

Why I conclude this
- Spatial concentration: the L2 norms are largest in middle-to-late layers (roughly layers 14–25) and concentrated at early token positions (pos1–pos4). That placement is exactly where residual-stream signals typically affect the next-token distribution, so the difference is behaviorally relevant.
- Logit-lens evidence: the top-scoring tokens for the highest-norm (layer,position) cells repeatedly include culinary/restaurant tokens (e.g., restaurant, Restaurant, Cooking, cooking, Chef, baking, kitchen, Cook, microwave, Cake, baked, oven) and professional/academic tokens (e.g., dissertation, professional/Professional, metropolitan, sciences, Innovation, technical, molecular, preventive). These clusters appear across many of the high-norm cells.
- Consistency across layers/positions: the food/cooking cluster appears strongly and repeatedly from ~layer 17 through ~25 at pos2–pos4, while “dissertation/professional” tokens are also recurrent across those layers. That repeated signal across many high-norm cells makes a random artifact or single-token idiosyncrasy unlikely.

Caveats / limits
- The logit-lens list also contains some noisy or isolated tokens (proper names, short fragments), so the signal is not perfectly clean.
- Patchscope continuations were not shown, so I can’t directly demonstrate that B actually outputs more cooking/professional content; the evidence is limited to residual activation differences and their decoded top token directions.
- I cannot name a precise training change or objective (e.g., “fine-tuned on restaurant reviews”) — only the interpretable lexical domains supported by the activation/readout evidence.

Short conclusion
- The most plausible, supported description is: Model B (relative to A) has increased residual-stream activation that biases next-token logits toward culinary/restaurant/cooking vocabulary and toward professional/academic vocabulary, concentrated in mid-to-late layers at early positions.
